question: Does Infinite Feature Selection supply a historically and mathematically defensible super-framework from which Transformer self-attention follows as a one-hop special case?

key_findings.claim: The manuscript proposes pairwise affinity computation as the common abstraction linking feature selection, sequence attention, non-local vision, and graph attention.
key_findings.evidence: The abstract and conclusion organize each family around a matrix A whose entries represent pairwise relations and whose downstream use modulates information flow.

key_findings.claim: Inf-FS is presented as a global feature-centrality method based on a discounted matrix power series.
key_findings.evidence: The manuscript defines S as the sum of α^k A^k and gives the resolvent (I−αA)^{-1}−I under α below the reciprocal spectral radius. Feature scores aggregate multi-hop walks before ranking and selecting columns.

key_findings.claim: Transformer self-attention is accurately summarized at a high level as row-normalized query-key affinities followed by value aggregation.
key_findings.evidence: Pages 8–9 give QK transpose scores, scaling, row-wise softmax, and a value-weighted output for every query position, while noting multi-head variants and quadratic sequence cost.

key_findings.claim: The central assertion is that self-attention is a one-hop special case and Inf-FS is therefore a superset framework.
key_findings.evidence: The manuscript repeatedly identifies an Inf-FS path-length-one operation with a single attention layer and states in the conclusion and comparison table that learned query-key attention is a subset of the Inf-FS formulation.

key_findings.claim: The claimed special-case relation is not established because the two maps have different codomains and operations.
key_findings.evidence: At one hop Inf-FS forms a scalar score per feature by summing an affinity row, whereas attention forms a distinct vector per query by multiplying normalized row weights by value vectors. Sharing a matrix-shaped intermediate does not make either complete computation a special case of the other, and the manuscript supplies no parameter mapping or equivalence theorem.

key_findings.claim: Identifying the softmax attention matrix with the Inf-FS adjacency makes the proposed one-hop selector degenerate.
key_findings.evidence: Every row of a softmax attention matrix sums to one. Inf-FS path-length-one scoring by row sum would therefore assign every token the same score, eliminating selection. Using raw QK transpose instead avoids that collapse but abandons nonnegative stochastic weights and provides no convergence guarantee for the power series.

key_findings.claim: Inf-FS and ordinary self-attention do not even share the same graph symmetry class.
key_findings.evidence: Inf-FS is described and implemented as an undirected feature graph with symmetric variance/correlation affinities. Query and key projections in self-attention are generally different, so QK transpose and its row-softmax are directed and asymmetric. The manuscript does not state constraints that would reconcile this mismatch.

key_findings.claim: Stacked attention layers are not powers of one fixed affinity matrix.
key_findings.evidence: Inf-FS sums powers of the same A. A Transformer recomputes a new attention matrix after every representation update and interleaves value projections, residual paths, normalization, feed-forward nonlinearities, and usually different parameters. Thus the manuscript's multi-hop analogy is only a metaphor, not the claimed matrix-power correspondence.

key_findings.claim: The comparison table attributes input-dynamic capabilities to Inf-FS that its own prose and cited primary methods do not provide.
key_findings.evidence: Pages 7, 15, and 16 correctly characterize classical Inf-FS as a static dataset-level ranking. Page 22 instead says its scores can be recomputed dynamically for each input sequence and calls the method a graph of features or tokens. The cited 2015 method computes variance and Spearman correlation across samples; the 2017 latent version learns one training-set feature graph, not token-wise per-example attention.

key_findings.claim: The account overstates full connectivity for Transformer decoders.
key_findings.evidence: It says each position in an encoder or decoder attends to all positions in the same sequence and repeatedly describes a fully connected token graph. Autoregressive decoder self-attention is causally masked; sparse and local Transformer variants also violate the claimed complete graph.

anchors.section: Emergence of self-attention in sequence models

key_findings.claim: The manuscript demonstrates structural resemblance but no historical transmission from Inf-FS to Transformer self-attention.
key_findings.evidence: It uses terms such as origin, pivotal, anticipated, and later adopted, yet gives no citation path, author testimony, shared personnel, or contemporaneous evidence that sequence-attention researchers knew Inf-FS. Attention Is All You Need does not cite Roffo or feature selection. Similar mathematical motifs alone cannot establish intellectual lineage.

key_findings.claim: The manuscript's own chronology weakens the claim that Inf-FS was the foundational origin.
key_findings.evidence: It records bilateral filtering, non-local means, PageRank, and a learned attentional feature-selection network before Inf-FS, and later concedes that non-local means already performs an affinity-weighted value average that is much closer to attention's actual input-output map. Bahdanau attention and the 2014 attentional neural network also predate the December 2015 Inf-FS publication.

key_findings.claim: The title and repeated origin language sit uneasily with the manuscript's narrower disclaimer.
key_findings.evidence: Page 3 says it does not claim Inf-FS introduced self-attention in its modern form, but the title calls the paper The Origin of Self-Attention and later prose says Inf-FS introduced a structure subsequently adopted by neural self-attention. No operational definition separates origin, anticipation, resemblance, and influence.

key_findings.claim: The paper is a narrative synthesis, not a reproducible survey or a mathematical result.
key_findings.evidence: There is no literature-search protocol, inclusion criterion, citation graph, theorem, proof, formal definition of the proposed paradigm, experiment, dataset, quantitative comparison, uncertainty analysis, or ablation. The sole original visual synthesis is a comparison table floated after the references.

key_findings.claim: The feature-selection interpretation conflates weighting, mixing, selection, and explanation.
key_findings.evidence: Softmax attention usually retains every token and mixes transformed values into query-specific outputs; it does not choose a global subset. Attention weights also need not measure causal feature importance. The manuscript nevertheless calls attention contextual feature selection and says GAT weights improve interpretability without engaging the established attention-as-explanation debate.

key_findings.claim: A cited arXiv identifier for an attention-based feature-selection paper resolves to an unrelated traffic-control paper.
key_findings.evidence: Reference 26 assigns arXiv:1811.03846 to Unsupervised Feature Selection Using Attention-Based Neural Networks by Roy, Charikar, and Singh. The official arXiv record is Computation Load Balancing Real-Time Model Predictive Control in Urban Traffic Networks by Zou, Lu, and Li.

key_findings.claim: A second cited arXiv identifier and author list for a feature-selection survey are unrelated to the claimed work.
key_findings.evidence: Reference 44 labels arXiv:2205.03466 as A Survey on Feature Selection Methods by R. Chandrashekar, M. Huang, and Q. Liu. The official record is a phylogenetics paper, The Tree of Blobs of a Species Network. The well-known feature-selection survey is a 2014 journal article by Girish Chandrashekar and Ferat Sahin.

key_findings.claim: The manuscript repeatedly misattributes AFS.
key_findings.evidence: References 27 and 34 list J. Gui, T. Liu, Z. Sun, D. Tao, and T. Tan. The official AAAI 2019 paper AFS: An Attention-Based Mechanism for Supervised Feature Selection is by Ning Gui, Danni Ge, and Ziyin Hu. The source file also defines the same AFS bibliography key twice.

key_findings.claim: Sequential Attention is cited under a nonexistent title and wrong authors.
key_findings.evidence: Reference 35 names T. Zhao, Q. Kong, and Y. Wang and calls the ICLR 2023 paper Sequential Self-Attention for Progressive Feature Selection. The official work is Sequential Attention for Feature Selection by Taisuke Yasuda and six coauthors, arXiv:2209.14881.

key_findings.claim: Reference 38 appears to be a fabricated hybrid of two real papers.
key_findings.evidence: It assigns An Attentional Neural Network for Image Classification, NeurIPS 2014 to Wang, Girshick, Gupta, and He, who authored Non-local Neural Networks in 2018. The actual NeurIPS 2014 attentional neural network is by Qian Wang, Jiaxing Zhang, Sen Song, and Zheng Zhang and has a different title.

key_findings.claim: The LatentGNN citation is also wrong in title, authors, and venue.
key_findings.evidence: Reference 43 lists Learning Node Representations with Latent Graphs by Liu, Lin, Li, Zhou, and Sun at NeurIPS 2019. The cited method is LatentGNN: Learning Efficient Non-local Relations for Visual Recognition by Songyang Zhang, Shipeng Yan, and Xuming He at ICML 2019, arXiv:1905.11634.

key_findings.claim: The bibliography has systematic duplication and weak editorial control.
key_findings.evidence: The source contains 61 bibliography entries but only 57 unique keys: Vaswani2017, Bahdanau2015, Gui2019, and Gui2019AFS are each defined twice. It also duplicates the Inf-FS, AFS, Bahdanau, and Transformer works as separately numbered references, includes an incomplete toolbox reference, and devotes roughly fifteen entries to the author's own work.

key_findings.claim: The arXiv reproducibility claims do not match the deposited revision.
key_findings.evidence: The official v2 landing page says 24 pages, 10 figures, and companion code and reproducibility materials. The hash-matched v2 PDF has 22 pages, no figures, and one table; the source archive contains only main.tex and 00README.json and names no companion artifact. The paper itself links a nonexistent github.com/giorgioroffo/inf-FS path.

key_findings.claim: The actual Inf-FS repository confirms a static dataset-level algorithm rather than the table's token-dynamic super-framework.
key_findings.evidence: The discoverable repository at github.com/giorgioroffo/Infinite-Feature-Selection, audited at commit ebaa33e7d7747caa13ec458752afb6da3ab3c545, contains two MATLAB functions. They build one feature-by-feature matrix from dataset-wide correlation, variance, mutual information, and class-separation statistics and return one global ranking. There are no token queries, keys, values, per-example weights, tests, or pinned environment.

key_findings.claim: The deposited revision carries inconsistent version labeling.
key_findings.evidence: The arXiv landing page and exact PDF hash identify v2, revised 26 July 2025, while page 1 still says Version 1, July 2025. This does not change the mathematical content but further reduces provenance clarity.

key_findings.claim: A 2026 follow-up by the author supplies the operator and experiments missing here.
key_findings.evidence: Self-Attention And Beyond the Infinite introduces Infinite Self-Attention as an explicit discounted Neumann series over content-adaptive token graphs, adds a linear approximation, and reports ImageNet, robustness, throughput, energy, and resolution results. This makes the 2025 paper best viewed as a motivating position piece, not the validated method.

key_findings.claim: The manuscript's defensible contribution is a readable cross-domain analogy, not an origin result.
key_findings.evidence: Its strongest material is the side-by-side vocabulary for global feature graphs, token attention, non-local vision, and graph message weighting. Once the unsupported historical influence, superset relation, interpretability, and dynamic Inf-FS claims are removed, the affinity-matrix lens remains useful pedagogically but is already present in closer kernel and geometric-deep-learning accounts.

method.core_idea: Construct a retrospective conceptual taxonomy around pairwise affinity matrices and argue that Infinite Feature Selection's graph resolvent generalizes the one-hop affinity aggregation used by self-attention.
method.mechanism: The manuscript narrates a chronology from psychological attention and early pairwise filters through graph centrality, Inf-FS, neural sequence attention, Transformers, non-local vision, and GATs. It compares how each constructs A, normalizes it, propagates through it, and produces scores or representations, then interprets neural attention and hard gates as context-dependent feature selection.
assumptions: A shared pairwise matrix is sufficient to define a meaningful algorithmic family.
Inf-FS permits arbitrary learned affinities and arbitrary element types, rather than being defined by its dataset-level feature graph and ranking output.
Path-length-one Inf-FS and attention value aggregation are the same graph operation despite different outputs.
Stacking input-dependent attention layers is adequately modeled by powers of a fixed adjacency.
Soft attention weights can be interpreted as feature importance or selection.
Structural resemblance is evidence of conceptual origin even without a citation or influence path.
The selected historical examples adequately cover earlier affinity-based computation.
Static undirected feature affinities and directed per-example token affinities can be compared without formal constraints.

techniques.role: Uses a pairwise matrix A as the common descriptive object across feature, token, pixel, and node models.
Explains Inf-FS importance as a discounted sum over all graph-walk lengths and its closed-form resolvent.
Maps one Inf-FS matrix power to one attention hop and deeper powers to stacked layers.
Orders psychological, signal-processing, graph-ranking, feature-selection, NLP, vision, and GNN precedents.
Translates features, tokens, spatial locations, and graph nodes into a shared node-edge vocabulary.
Interprets attention and gates as differentiable, instance-conditioned extensions of feature selection.
Contrasts graph type, pairwise score, normalization, depth, output, learnability, and goal.
Relates classical non-local averaging and learned non-local blocks to attention-weighted value aggregation.
Frames GAT as learning a sparse feature-dependent adjacency and Transformer attention as its complete-graph analogue.

evaluations.setting: Author evidence across the entire 22-page manuscript
evaluations.metric: Presence of original theorem, proof, quantitative experiment, dataset, or systematic-review protocol
evaluations.result: None is provided; the paper is a narrative position and synthesis article.
evaluations.baseline: Standards expected for a mathematical special-case claim, an empirical methods paper, or a reproducible systematic history.

evaluations.setting: Type and algebra audit of the claimed Inf-FS-to-attention reduction
evaluations.metric: Existence of a parameter mapping preserving inputs, outputs, normalization, directionality, and composition
evaluations.result: No reduction is supplied; one-hop Inf-FS outputs scalar row sums while attention outputs query-specific value vectors, and softmax row sums collapse the proposed Inf-FS score.
evaluations.baseline: Direct equality or an explicit theorem showing self-attention as a constrained Inf-FS operator.

evaluations.metric: Whether Inf-FS predates closer learned or affinity-weighted aggregation mechanisms
evaluations.result: It does not: bilateral and non-local weighted averages, Bahdanau attention, and the 2014 attentional neural network predate the 2015 Inf-FS paper.
evaluations.baseline: A historical-origin claim supported by temporal priority and evidence of transmission.

evaluations.metric: Resolvable identifiers, correct titles/authors/venues, unique bibliography keys, and support for cited claims
evaluations.result: Multiple references are unrelated, misattributed, duplicated, incomplete, or apparently hybridized; two claimed arXiv IDs resolve to unrelated traffic-control and phylogenetics papers.
evaluations.baseline: Official arXiv, AAAI, CVF, ICML, NeurIPS, and publisher records checked through 2026-08-23.

evaluations.setting: Exact arXiv v2 PDF and source archive
evaluations.metric: Agreement with landing-page claims of 24 pages, 10 figures, code, and reproducibility materials
evaluations.result: The deposited PDF has 22 pages, zero figures, and one table; the archive contains only main.tex and 00README.json and gives no companion artifact.
evaluations.baseline: Official arXiv v2 metadata and source bundle.

evaluations.setting: Public Inf-FS artifact at commit ebaa33e7d7747caa13ec458752afb6da3ab3c545
evaluations.metric: Support for dynamic per-input token affinities and executable reproducibility
evaluations.result: Two MATLAB routines implement static dataset-level feature matrices and one global ranking. The cited repository URL is dead, and the discoverable repository has no tests or pinned environment.
evaluations.baseline: The manuscript's page-22 claim that Inf-FS scores can be dynamic and recomputed for every input sequence.

evaluations.metric: Whether the proposed affinity-resolvent bridge has subsequently been made operational
evaluations.result: The author's 2026 Infinite Self-Attention follow-up explicitly defines a content-adaptive Neumann operator, linear approximation, and empirical evaluation, supplying elements absent from the reviewed manuscript.

limitations: No formal definition of affinity-based computation or of what counts as a special case.
No theorem, proof, or type-correct reduction from Transformer attention to Inf-FS.
No experiment validates the proposed equivalence or any practical consequence.
No systematic-search method or inclusion criteria support the historical narrative.
No citation-network or archival evidence establishes intellectual influence.
The narrative centers the author's own method despite multiple closer and earlier mechanisms.
It conflates static feature ranking, dynamic value mixing, gating, and hard subset selection.
It does not address asymmetry, causal masking, positional encoding in the formal comparison, residual paths, or layerwise changes of A.
It treats attention weights as interpretable importance without the necessary causal qualification.
The bibliography contains numerous material errors and duplicate entries.
ArXiv comments about figures and companion materials are inconsistent with the deposited source.
The linked Inf-FS repository path is nonexistent and the actual code lacks tests and environment pins.
failure_modes: A matrix-shape analogy can be mistaken for functional equivalence when the operators have different outputs.
Substituting a row-stochastic attention matrix into Inf-FS one-hop centrality yields uniform scores.
Substituting raw directed query-key scores into an undirected nonnegative graph resolvent can break its interpretation and convergence.
Treating stacked attention as powers of one A erases parameter changes and nonlinear state dependence.
Calling soft weighting selection can falsely imply sparsity, deletion, or causal importance.
A title framed as origin can be read as priority even after a narrow disclaimer.
Incorrect identifiers can make a literature graph appear supported while pointing to unrelated fields.
Self-citation concentration can bias which historical branch receives foundational status.
Static code can be generalized in prose into a dynamic framework that it never implements.
Stale arXiv comments can overstate the available evidence and reproducibility package.
reusable_insights: Pairwise affinity plus aggregation is a productive cross-domain design vocabulary.
Any claimed operator inclusion should specify domains, codomains, parameter restrictions, normalization, and a constructive mapping.
Row-sum invariants are a fast sanity check when comparing graph centrality with softmax attention.
Directedness and symmetry distinguish query-key attention from classical undirected feature graphs.
Multi-hop claims must separate powers of one fixed transition matrix from products of state-dependent layer operators.
Non-local filtering is a closer historical analogue to attention when both compute affinity-weighted values.
Historical priority, conceptual resemblance, and documented influence should be reported as separate relations.
Feature weighting, feature selection, message passing, and explanation need distinct terminology.
Source-archive and bibliography audits can materially change the credibility of a conceptual paper.
The 2026 InfSA follow-up suggests a testable research direction: compare fixed resolvents, layerwise products, and recurrent content-adaptive diffusion under matched compute.
open_questions: Can one define a minimal typed affinity-operator calculus that truly contains Inf-FS, attention, kernels, non-local filtering, and graph message passing?
What exact restrictions make a resolvent over token affinities equivalent or approximately equivalent to repeated attention?
How should the transition operator be normalized when affinities are directed, signed, masked, or input-dependent?
Can attention-derived centrality predict ablation-based causal importance better than raw attention weights?
When does a content-adaptive Neumann series improve accuracy or long-range reasoning under matched compute?
How do causal masks and positional encodings change the graph-diffusion interpretation?
Can citation-network and archival evidence produce a less author-centered history of self-attention?
Do dynamic per-example feature graphs offer benefits beyond established TabNet, Sequential Attention, and active feature-acquisition methods?
Can the 2026 Infinite Self-Attention claims be independently reproduced with complete training recipes and modern baselines?
Which conclusions survive if feature selection is reserved for actual sparse support rather than dense value mixing?

competitive_landscape.title: Infinite Feature Selection
competitive_landscape.relationship: The primary method on which the reviewed paper bases its origin and superset thesis.
competitive_landscape.difference: The accepted ICCV paper defines an undirected dataset-level feature graph from standard deviation and Spearman correlation, computes one global resolvent ranking, and evaluates feature selection. It does not define arbitrary token operators, per-example affinities, query-key-value aggregation, or self-attention.

competitive_landscape.title: Infinite Latent Feature Selection: A Probabilistic Latent Graph-Based Ranking Approach
competitive_landscape.relationship: Learned-affinity extension invoked to broaden Inf-FS beyond its original handcrafted graph.
competitive_landscape.difference: ILFS learns one training-set feature graph with a supervised PLSA-inspired model and still returns a global feature ranking. It is learned but not dynamically recomputed as token self-attention for each input.

competitive_landscape.title: Infinite Feature Selection: A Graph-based Feature Filtering Approach
competitive_landscape.relationship: Mature Inf-FS framework and Markov-chain account cited as evidence for general affinity-based ranking.
competitive_landscape.difference: It supports customizable dataset-level feature relations, supervised and unsupervised rankings, and empirical benchmarks, but remains a filtering operator rather than a Transformer layer.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
competitive_landscape.relationship: Earlier learned compatibility-and-weighted-value mechanism in neural sequence modeling.
competitive_landscape.difference: Bahdanau attention is cross-attention rather than self-attention, but its input-dependent learned weights and value aggregation are functionally closer to Transformer attention and predate Inf-FS.

competitive_landscape.title: Attentional Neural Network: Feature Selection Using Cognitive Feedback
competitive_landscape.relationship: Earlier neural feature-selection mechanism already framed explicitly as attention.
competitive_landscape.difference: It uses top-down cognitive bias to gate learned features and was published at NeurIPS 2014, directly weakening the claim that 2015 Inf-FS first established attention-like feature weighting.

competitive_landscape.title: Long Short-Term Memory-Networks for Machine Reading
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct recurrent self-attention precursor.
competitive_landscape.difference: It explicitly lets sequence positions attend within a memory-augmented recurrent model; unlike Inf-FS, it is input-conditioned and produces contextual sequence representations.

competitive_landscape.title: A Structured Self-attentive Sentence Embedding
competitive_landscape.relationship: Pre-Transformer work explicitly using multiple learned self-attention views over a sentence.
competitive_landscape.difference: It provides an actual neural self-attention operator and empirical task evaluation, whereas the reviewed manuscript retroactively groups such operators under Inf-FS without an equivalence proof.

competitive_landscape.title: Attention Is All You Need
competitive_landscape.relationship: The canonical Transformer self-attention formulation being reinterpreted.
competitive_landscape.difference: It defines learned query, key, and value projections, masks, multi-head aggregation, residual blocks, and end-to-end experiments. It does not cite Inf-FS, so it supports functional comparison but not historical transmission.

competitive_landscape.title: Non-local Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: A closer general operator that explicitly treats self-attention as a special case of non-local weighted aggregation.
competitive_landscape.difference: The non-local family preserves attention's pairwise weight-and-value output and explores several affinity functions with experiments. It therefore substantiates a super-family relation more directly than Inf-FS scalar centrality does.

competitive_landscape.title: Graph Attention Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Sparse graph message-passing instantiation of learned attention.
competitive_landscape.difference: GAT learns directed neighbor-specific coefficients and aggregates transformed node values on a supplied graph; it offers a direct message-passing formalism rather than Inf-FS global ranking.

competitive_landscape.title: Set Transformer: A Framework for Attention-based Permutation-Invariant Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Attention framework for unordered sets, close to the paper's element-agnostic affinity thesis.
competitive_landscape.difference: It supplies permutation-equivariant/invariant constructions, induced attention for scalability, theory, and experiments; the reviewed paper provides only a post hoc analogy.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformer Dissection: A Unified Understanding of Transformer's Attention via the Lens of Kernel
competitive_landscape.relationship: Established unifying account of attention as kernel smoothing over inputs.
competitive_landscape.difference: The kernel view is type-aligned with normalized affinity-weighted values and yields new attention compositions plus experiments. It is a closer and better validated unification than feature-centrality ranking.

competitive_landscape.title: Attention is not Explanation
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct challenge to the manuscript's interpretation of attention weights as importance and interpretability.
competitive_landscape.difference: It empirically finds attention weights can diverge from gradient importance and can change without changing outputs, showing why dense attention should not automatically be called feature selection or explanation.

competitive_landscape.title: Concrete Autoencoders for Differentiable Feature Selection and Reconstruction
competitive_landscape.relationship: Differentiable hard feature-selection baseline.
competitive_landscape.difference: Concrete selectors learn an actual discrete subset through a continuous relaxation, clarifying the distinction between selecting support and densely mixing every token with soft attention.

competitive_landscape.title: Hopfield Networks is All You Need
competitive_landscape.relationship: Formal connection between attention and associative-memory energy dynamics.
competitive_landscape.difference: It derives an explicit equivalence to modern Hopfield updates, analyzes convergence and storage, and evaluates models; the reviewed paper offers no comparable derivation for Inf-FS.

competitive_landscape.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Historical and formal predecessor account tying linear attention to 1990s fast-weight programming.
competitive_landscape.difference: It proves an operator equivalence and tests improved update rules, providing both historical evidence and mathematics absent from the Inf-FS origin narrative.

competitive_landscape.title: Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges
competitive_landscape.relationship: Broad established framework positioning attention inside message passing and latent graph inference.
competitive_landscape.difference: It states Transformers can be posed exactly as attentional GNNs over a complete graph while carefully treating equivariance and positional information. This is more formal and less method-specific than the reviewed affinity taxonomy.

competitive_landscape.title: Sequential Attention for Feature Selection
competitive_landscape.relationship: Actual ICLR 2023 attention-based feature-selection work that the manuscript attempts to cite.
competitive_landscape.difference: It uses attention weights as a greedy forward-selection proxy, relates a linear version to orthogonal matching pursuit, and evaluates feature subsets. The reviewed bibliography gives it the wrong title and authors.

competitive_landscape.title: The underlying structures of self-attention: symmetry, directionality, and emergent dynamics in Transformer training
competitive_landscape.relationship: Contemporary mathematical analysis of attention matrices across objectives and modalities.
competitive_landscape.difference: It derives and validates how bidirectional and autoregressive objectives induce different symmetry and directionality, properties ignored by a comparison based on undirected Inf-FS affinities.

competitive_landscape.title: Self-Attention And Beyond the Infinite: Towards Linear Transformers with Infinite Self-Attention
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct 2026 follow-up by the reviewed paper's author that operationalizes the proposed bridge.
competitive_landscape.difference: It defines an actual content-adaptive Neumann diffusion operator, derives a linear approximation, and reports ImageNet, shift, throughput, energy, eigenvector-match, and extreme-resolution results. Those formal and empirical contributions are absent from the 2025 position paper.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a cross-domain historical and mathematical reframing in which Inf-FS is a flexible affinity-computation superset and Transformer self-attention is its dynamic one-hop special case.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The manuscript gathers feature graphs, attention, non-local vision, and GATs into one vocabulary and supplies a broad chronology plus a comparison table. However, kernel, non-local, message-passing, Hopfield, and fast-weight accounts already offer closer or formally demonstrated unifications. The central Inf-FS inclusion fails a type and normalization audit, no influence chain is shown, there is no original experiment or proof, and the bibliography and artifact metadata contain material errors.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Novelty is modest as a pedagogical position piece and low as either a history or mathematical result. Its useful residue is the prompt to compare global graph centrality with contextual attention. The defensible new research program appears only in the 2026 Infinite Self-Attention follow-up, where a content-adaptive resolvent is explicitly defined and evaluated.

reviewer_notes: All 22 pages were read in full and rendered; every displayed equation and the sole table on page 22 were visually inspected. The exact arXiv v2 source archive was audited and contains only main.tex and 00README.json, despite landing-page comments claiming 24 pages, 10 figures, and companion reproducibility materials. Every bibliography entry was inspected; suspicious identifiers, titles, authors, and venues were checked against primary arXiv, CVF, AAAI, NeurIPS, ICML, and publisher records. The original Inf-FS and ILFS papers were read at their method equations. The dead cited GitHub path and the discoverable Inf-FS repository were audited; commit ebaa33e7d7747caa13ec458752afb6da3ab3c545 confirms static global MATLAB ranking. Current primary competitors and the direct 2026 follow-up were checked through 2026-08-23. No shared projections were rebuilt.
